overall: Atlanta is starting the day with unexpectedly persistent overcast conditions — a 100% cloud fraction with a very low ceiling of 335m (roughly 1,100 ft) — which is significantly suppressing solar heating despite it being mid-morning. The temperature has only climbed to 75.2°F by 11:09 AM ET, which is well below what would be expected on a day forecast to reach 88°F. The warming velocity of +1.8°F/hr is modest, though a recent 30-minute spike to +3.6°F/hr suggests some intermittent cloud breaks may be occurring. High humidity (dewpoint ~70°F) is also constraining the heating ceiling.
forecast_obs_notes: There is a notable divergence between the NWS official forecast (88°F, 'mostly sunny') and current observations (OVC, 100% cloud cover). NWP models are also warmer than the observed trajectory implies: ECMWF=85.5, NBM=86.2, HRRR=83.9 — all well above the ~81-82°F that a simple linear extrapolation from current conditions would yield (~75.2°F + 1.8°F/hr × ~3.5 hrs to peak). The META fused model centers its probability mass in the 84-85°F bucket (29.7%), with INTRADAY spreading mass flatly across 84-89°F, reflecting genuine uncertainty about whether the overcast clears sufficiently.
max_temp_prediction: The outcome hinges almost entirely on whether the overcast breaks before the peak heating window (roughly 13:00–16:00 ET). If clouds persist, the high will likely top out near 80-83°F; if they clear by early afternoon as NWP models implicitly assume, the high could reach 84-87°F. The NWS 88°F forecast appears optimistic given the current OVC suppression and high dewpoints limiting latent heat. Weighing the NWP consensus (~85°F), the META model's modal bucket (84-85°F), and the current cloud suppression, a high near 85°F is the best central estimate with moderate-low confidence given cloud timing uncertainty.
